title: Gufta

paragraphs: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Gufta, Maaserot, chapter 1, at the end of halakhah 4. Hyman suggests it is a town name: in Sanhedrin, chapter 10, halakhah 2, we find Menachem, a man of Gufta, and in Megillah, chapter 3, halakhah 7, Rabbi Yonatan, the scribe of Gufta.[^1]

notes.text: The town-name explanation is Hyman’s inference. סה״ד means “at the end of halakhah 4.”
